daily.title: ITAT Holds Presumptive Taxation Under Section 44AD Does Not Exempt Assessee from Maintaining Books
daily.summary: The ITAT holds cash deposits of Rs. 47.24 lakh as unexplained despite earlier bank withdrawals. The assessee is Rameshbhai Bhikhabhai Bajaniya who filed his return of income for Assessment Year 2017-18 under the presumptive taxation scheme provided under Section 44AD of the Income Tax Act . During the assessment proceedings, the AO noticed cash deposits aggregating to Rs. 47,24,000 in the assessee's ICICI Bank account during the demonetisation period. The AO treated the deposits as unexplained cash credits under Section 68 of the Act.

daily.title: Ethanol policy reset: What does the shift in feedstock priorities mean for sugar mills and farmers?
daily.summary: Policy shift restricts sugar-based ethanol, urging a balanced, predictable framework that protects sugar stocks while steering mills and farmers through grain- and molasses-led supply. The Government has directed zero diversion of sugar towards ethanol production. The Oil Marketing Companies’ tender for approximately 1,100 crore litres excludes ethanol produced from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses, leaving C-heavy molasses as the only eligible sugarcane-based feedstock. The decision follows concerns over tightening domestic sugar availability. The 2025-26 season ended with stocks of approximately 35 lakh tonnes, the lowest in nearly three decades.

daily.title: ITAT Pune Grants Section 80G Approval Where Actual Religious Expenditure Is Within 5% Limit
daily.summary: ITAT Pune grants Section 80G approval after finding actual religious expenditure below the 5% limit despite its classification in audited accounts. Summary: The Pune Bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) held that recognition under Section 80G of the Income-tax Act, 1961 cannot be denied merely because expenditure has been classified as religious expenditure in the Income and Expenditure Account, when its actual nature is predominantly charitable and the expenditure genuinely incurred for religious purposes is within the statutory limit. daily.summary: The ITAT has held that Ad Hoc addition under Section 41(1) was prejudicial to the assessee and not Revenue. Aggrieved by the revisionary order, the assessee approached the Tribunal, contending that the PCIT had wrongly assumed jurisdiction under Section 263. The Tribunal observed that the PCIT had correctly recognised that the Income Tax Act does not permit an ad hoc disallowance of a fixed percentage of total sundry creditors. The Tribunal explained that sundry creditors represent liabilities appearing in the balance sheet and not current-year income or expenditure.
